title: Operational runway restoration and threshold recalibration for dedicated capacity shortfall
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: During a multi-region traffic surge on 2026-02-28 we observed a progressive headroom collapse in several Dedicated pools leading to sustained request throttling for a subset of high-throughput customers. This ticket coordinates the incident runbook closure activities, the short-term runway-restoration actions, and a set of threshold/heuristic recalibrations to prevent recurrence.

Scope: The work covers triage artifacts, short-term mitigations that restore customer-facing throughput, instrumentation gaps uncovered during the incident, an RCA, and a prioritized set of engineering tasks for long-term resilience (control plane policies, autoscaler tuning, and capacity reservation logic).

Goals: (1) Restore deterministic runway and avoid future multi-pool headroom collapse under similar load patterns. (2) Adjust autoscaler thresholds and backoff to tolerate bursty tail loads while preserving SLOs. (3) Codify new observability signals and automatic mitigations into the runbook and the orchestration layer.

High-level technical findings: (a) A change to the predictive autoscaler weighting reduced lookahead margin for large-tenancy pools by ~40%, amplifying allocation lag during burst growth. (b) The request routing fallback had an optimistic compatibility check that caused delayed failover for pools with mixed model variants. (c) KV-cache warmup delays increased effective per-request latency under scaling events, reducing effective throughput and masking headroom until throttles engaged.

Deliverables: (1) emergency stabilizer PRs (autoscaler hotfix + routing fallback patch), (2) updated runbook with explicit runway validation and emergency reservation procedure, (3) telemetry dashboards and new synthetic tests for headroom drift, (4) RFC for permanent autoscaler redesign and reservation guardrail, (5) postmortem with corrective action tracker and owners.
acceptance_criteria: Emergency stabilizer hotfixes merged and deployed to production with verified rollback path
Runbook updated with step-by-step runway validation and contact matrix; tested in a tabletop exercise
New headroom drift dashboard created and a synthetic canary that simulates sustained burst loads
Autoscaler threshold and lookahead tuning documented and validated in canary regions with observed improvements in median scaling latency
RCA published with prioritized action items assigned and timelines for long-term fixes

notes: Operational note: During the incident we discovered that bursts from a small number of heavy-tenancy customers can cause non-linear headroom degradation; mitigation requires both faster scale-up and temporary soft-throttling at tenant-level to preserve pool health.
Trade-offs considered: Increasing reserved headroom reduces utilization and unit economics; the proposed reservation guardrail will be conditional and time-limited to minimize cost impact.
Follow-up: Evaluate predictive autoscaler using a richer feature set (per-tenant token burn patterns, KV-cache warmup state) before changing global weights again.
